newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal at second highest record--AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal at second highest record--AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic as measured in intermodal reached the second highest weekly total on record, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
AAR said that for the week ended October 26, intermodal traffic, at 178,487 trailers and containers, was 1.2 percent below the record 180,734 set the week ended September 28.
Intermodal in the October 26 week was up 4.8 percent from 170,234 loadings in the year-ago week. Intermodal traffic does not include carloads.
AAR said carloads in the week totaled 354,831, a 1.1 percent increase from 351,005 a year ago.
Ton-miles in the week also rose 1.9 percent to 26.6 billion from 26.1 billion last year. A ton-mile is equal to one ton of freight hauled one mile.
"The fourth quarter always brings a surge in intermodal loadings as stores stock up for the holiday buying season, and that is happening again this year," Harvey Levine, AAR chief economist, said.

Levine also noted that grain loadings in the week, at 29,309, were 4.4 percent above 28,063 in the year-ago week. "But for the first 43 weeks of this year, grain is still down more than 12 percent on a cumulative basis compared with last year," he added.
AAR said that carloads of lumber and wood products rose 6.2 percent to 5,614 from 5,284 a year ago, while metals and metal products increased 8.7 percent to 12,945 carloads from 11,914.

Coal loadings were up 3.4 percent in the week to 133,848 from 129,385 in the year-ago week, and grain mill products rose 4.6 percent to 9,910 carloads from 9,473. Loadings of petroleum products stood at 5,633, up 3.2 percent from 5,458 a year ago, it said.

But farm products other than grain fell 6.2 percent to 2,433 loadings from 2,593 a year ago, while metallic ores decreased 9.6 percent to 16,849 carloads from 18,629. Primary forest products also fell by 11.3 percent to 7,869 carloads from 8,873 last year, AAR said.
In the first 43 weeks of 1996, AAR said ton-miles rose two percent from the same period last year. Intermodal traffic also rose 1.3 percent, but carloads fell 0.7 percent, AAR said.
